procedure.description: posterior lumbar interbody fusion, L4-L5, with decompression

denial.carcText: These are non-covered services because this is not deemed a 'medical necessity' by the payer.
denial.text: Silverline Medicare Advantage denied the claim for CPT 22630 (posterior lumbar interbody fusion, L4-L5, with decompression) with date of service 2026-05-19. CARC 50: These are non-covered services because this is not deemed a 'medical necessity' by the payer. Payer remark: Documentation does not demonstrate instability requiring fusion; decompression alone would be the covered procedure.

criteria.text: Failure of at least 6 months of conservative treatment including physical therapy, anti-inflammatory or analgesic medication, activity modification, and at least one epidural steroid injection.

Imaging documenting segmental instability or spondylolisthesis at the level to be fused: anterolisthesis of 3 millimeters or more, or translation of 4 millimeters or more or angulation of 10 degrees or more on flexion-extension radiographs, with stenosis or radiculopathy correlating with the symptoms.
Symptoms and examination findings correlate with the imaging level: radicular leg pain or neurogenic claudication with a corresponding dermatomal deficit.
Psychosocial screening completed with no untreated major depression or active substance use disorder, and nicotine-free or documented cessation of at least 6 weeks.

chart.text: She called asking about travel vaccines for a trip in early summer. Advised hepatitis A and a typhoid booster, referred to the travel clinic. Nothing else needed from us.
Gastroenterology note received. Screening colonoscopy completed, two small polyps removed, benign on pathology, repeat in 10 years.
From the referring physician: please evaluate and treat as you see fit. We have exhausted what we can do in primary care and the patient is motivated. Recent labs enclosed, all within normal limits.

Low back strain after moving furniture over the weekend. No radiation down the legs, no numbness, no bowel or bladder trouble. Paraspinal tenderness, straight leg raise negative. Heat, keep moving, ibuprofen with food for a week. Should settle.

66 year old woman in spine clinic with low back and leg pain going back about 3 years, much worse this past year. Drives a delivery route. Reviewed the imaging with her and the options from more therapy to decompression to fusion. Her history otherwise: migraines, rare now, hypothyroidism on levothyroxine. Allergies: penicillin, rash. Quit smoking 14 years ago, no alcohol, works two jobs. Family history noncontributory for what we are talking about today. She has been on meloxicam 15 daily and gabapentin 600 three times daily, stopped lifting at work, and did a course of PT last year. Bilateral leg pain into the lateral calves and the tops of the feet with standing and walking, walks about 200 feet before she has to sit, better leaning on the cart. L5 distribution. Extensor hallucis longus 4 out of 5 on the right, reflexes symmetric, straight leg raise negative.
Work note requested for a sick day last Monday. Faxed to the employer.

MRI lumbar spine without contrast. L4-L5: grade 1 degenerative anterolisthesis measuring 5 millimeters, facet effusions, severe central and bilateral lateral recess stenosis compressing the traversing L5 roots. L3-L4 and L5-S1 mild degenerative change without stenosis.

Knee pain going down stairs, left side, no injury, no locking or giving way. Patellar grind positive, no effusion, ligaments stable. Patellofemoral pain. Quad strengthening sheet, ice after activity, cushioned shoes.
Spine PT evaluation. Flexion-based program, core stabilization, nerve glides. Plan 12 weeks, twice a week.
Lumbar flexion-extension lateral radiographs. L4-L5: 6 millimeters of translation between flexion and extension, 10 degrees of angular motion. Other levels stable.
Session 2. Continued the program from the evaluation, tolerated well, home exercises reviewed, she reports no real change.

Twisted the left ankle stepping off a curb 4 days ago. Swelling over the lateral malleolus, tender over the ATFL, can bear weight. Ottawa negative, no film. Brace, ice, ibuprofen, elevate. Should be fine in a couple weeks.
Session 3. Continued the program from the evaluation, tolerated well, home exercises reviewed, she reports about the same.
Optometry report forwarded for the record. Routine refraction, mild astigmatism, new glasses prescribed, retinas healthy, pressures 19 and 14. No ocular pathology noted.
Session 4. Continued the program from the evaluation, tolerated well, home exercises reviewed, she reports no real change.
Pharmacy called about the refill on the omeprazole 40. Approved 90 days. She mentioned the heartburn is better since cutting back on coffee.
Session 5. Continued the program from the evaluation, tolerated well, home exercises reviewed, she reports slight improvement that does not last.
Session 6. Continued the program from the evaluation, tolerated well, home exercises reviewed, she reports about the same.

Trouble sleeping for a couple of months, falls asleep fine but wakes at three and lies there. No snoring per the spouse, no daytime naps, two cups of coffee before noon. Went over sleep hygiene, no screens in bed, cut the afternoon caffeine. Will hold off on medication for now.
Thyroid labs back. TSH 2.4, free T4 normal. No change to the levothyroxine 100. Repeat in a year.
Fluoroscopically guided transforaminal epidural steroid injection, L4-L5 right. Tolerated well.

Here with a cough and congestion for 8 days, low grade temp at home, no shortness of breath. Lungs clear, throat a little red, ears fine. Looks viral. Fluids, rest, honey for the cough, come back if she gets a fever over 101 or it goes past two weeks.
Patient called about a tick bite on the shoulder after a hike. Tick removed whole, no rash, no fever. Watch for a bull's-eye rash or flu symptoms over the next month and call if either shows up.
Blood pressure check. 131 over 80 today, 132 over 81 on repeat. She has been taking the lisinopril 20 most days, admits to missing weekends. Low salt talk again. Keep the dose, recheck in 12 weeks.

Annual physical. Feels well overall. Sleeping fine, appetite fine, no chest pain, no shortness of breath. Flu shot given in the left arm today. Due for a tetanus booster, she will think about it. Labs ordered, fasting.
Seasonal allergies acting up, itchy eyes, sneezing, clear drainage, worse outdoors. No wheeze. Cetirizine at night and the saline rinse. Fine with that.
Second transforaminal epidural steroid injection, L4-L5 right. The first gave about 2 weeks of relief.

Back to decide. Symptoms unchanged, walking distance down to about 150 feet. Recommended L4-L5 decompression and interbody fusion given the slip and the motion on the films. Risks reviewed at length. Vitals today 114 over 68, pulse 85. Finished 12 weeks of PT, two epidurals with transient relief only, still on the meloxicam and gabapentin. That is 8 months of conservative care without durable benefit. PHQ-9 score 5, no substance use, never smoked. Realistic expectations about what fusion will and will not fix.
Dermatology consult note received. Two actinic keratoses on the forehead treated with cryotherapy. Annual skin check recommended, sunscreen counseling done.
Burning with urination for two days, going frequently, no fever, no back pain. Urine dip positive for leukocytes and nitrites. Nitrofurantoin for five days, push fluids, call if fever or flank pain.

Ear fullness and muffled hearing on the left for a week after a cold. Canal clear, drum dull with fluid behind it, no infection. Serous otitis. Decongestant, swallow and yawn, recheck in three weeks if not better.
Interval visit. Nothing new since last time, symptoms as described before, she is managing. Went over the plan again and answered questions from her spouse.
Letter from the dentist's office confirming routine cleaning and exam completed, no active infection, no dental work pending. Sent at our request for the surgical file.
Nurse call. Patient had questions about time off work and whether she needs someone at home the first night. Answered both, she will arrange it.
Pre-op. Medical clearance in the chart, A1c 6.1, stopped the meloxicam. Consent signed for L4-L5 posterior lumbar interbody fusion with instrumentation.

expected.note: The chart documents every criterion; the CARC 50 denial can be answered from the record.
